title: Rose geranium room spray
subtitle: A light floral misting spray for rooms and soft furnishings
excerpt: Rose geranium room spray is a light misting spray made from distilled water, isopropyl alcohol, and rose geranium essential oil. Sprayed into the air or onto soft furnishings, it disperses in a few minutes and leaves a fresh, green-rosy scent. Makes 100 ml in a glass spray bottle; keeps six months.
sourceNotes: Rose geranium (Pelargonium graveolens) essential oil: flash point approximately 73°C (supplier SDS, New Directions Aromatics 2022). Isopropyl alcohol as a room spray carrier: solubilises the essential oil and prevents the spray nozzle from clogging with oil droplets. Room spray formulation: The Complete Book of Essential Oils and Aromatherapy by Valerie Wormwood (1991).

recipe.batchNotes: Scale up and bottle in multiple 100 ml spray bottles.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ready to use immediately. Shake before each use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Six months at room temperature. The isopropyl alcohol and essential oil are both stable; the distilled water is the limiting factor. Discard if the spray turns cloudy or develops any smell other than the rose geranium note.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which an essential oil can ignite if exposed to an open flame. Rose geranium essential oil has a flash point above 70°C, safe for room spray use. Do not spray directly onto candle flames or hot light bulbs.

content.text: Pour the isopropyl alcohol into the spray bottle first. Add the essential oil drops and swirl gently to dissolve. Add the distilled water. Seal and shake. The spray may appear slightly cloudy, this is the essential oil dispersing in the water-alcohol mixture and is normal.

Shake the bottle, then spray into the air at ceiling height or onto soft furnishings from 30 cm away. Two to three spritzes is enough for a medium room. The scent dissipates within ten to fifteen minutes to a fresher background note.
Six months at room temperature. Shake before each use. Keep away from heat sources and direct sunlight.
